title: Bptf loss drives a posterior neuronal Grk4/Zcwpw2/Resp18 chromatin-response that opposes Chd4 on diagnostic genes
exact_observed_result: Bptf perturbation drove Zcwpw2 and Grk4 up with Resp18, Abhd14b, and Stxbp2 down in 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA. In 151 and 155, Chd4 was the most negative restricted-signature neighbor of the Bptf FDR gene set.
biological_interpretation: BPTF/NURF loss defines a posterior neuronal chromatin-response branch that is not equivalent to CHD4/NuRD direction; both are chromatin remodeler-associated, but they push diagnostic Bptf genes in opposite directions.

support.description: The core Bptf branch repeats across three posterior classes and opposes Chd4 in the two strongest Bptf contexts; Resp18 is a narrow Atrx/Bptf/Trrap convergence marker.

caveats: Many Bptf-responsive rows were summarized at FDR<0.1, so the story relies on the diagnostic FDR<0.05 core rather than every tail gene.
The Chd4 opposition is a restricted-signature projection and does not imply a direct biochemical antagonism.
Atrx convergence is only marker-level on Resp18, not a broad phenocopy.

prior_expectation.summary: BPTF is the large NURF subunit and reads H3K4me3 through its PHD finger, whereas CHD4 is part of the NuRD remodeling complex; these priors support chromatin involvement but not the observed opposite direction.

citations.citation: Low et al., Journal of Biological Chemistry, 2016.
